# How to read

Under each question there is a `- [ ] A:` line.

- **Tick it without writing anything:** you agree with the proposal.
- **Tick it and add a detail:** you agree, with that detail.
- **Leave it unticked and write:** I revise the proposal.

Nothing here is built yet. The plan is in `docs/PLAN.md` (milestones J6 to J9).

# Where we are

- Joma is a normal window. Closing it hides it in `special:joma`, so it keeps running.
- The bar shows a separate QML plugin, which talks to Joma through `joma quick --json`.
- It has its own dropdown: contacts, quick chat, and call, share and file buttons.
- Installing takes three steps:
  1. `scripts/install.sh` puts the binary, icons and launcher in place;
  2. the plugin is linked into `~/.config/omarchy/plugins` by hand;
  3. the Super+Alt+M binding is added to `bindings.lua` by hand.
- Joma does not start at login. It manages one account only, and nothing else (no
  contacts, chats or profile) beyond what the chat view offers.

# A. Living in the bar

The idea: when Joma starts, it shows nothing but its icon in the bar. Clicking the icon
drops a panel down from the bar. A button in the panel pops the full window out; a button
in the full window pops it back into the bar.

**Q1. Draw the dropdown panel with Joma itself (GPUI), not with the QML plugin.**

> Decided in chat (2026-10-29): no plugin. Joma lives in the system tray like Signal
> (status dot, menu); a click or Super+Alt+M opens a compact floating window under the
> bar, which pops out to the full window. Built in 0.4.0-rc.1
> (`docs/design/05-tray-and-panel.md`).

Zed's GPUI can now open Wayland layer-shell surfaces (`WindowKind::LayerShell`), the
same kind of surface the Omarchy bar and its panels use. Joma can therefore draw a panel
anchored under the bar, at the right edge, above the other windows.

- One interface, one codebase: the panel and the full window share views, theme, input
  and keyboard shortcuts. The quick chat is the real chat (history, files, typing),
  not a reduced copy over the socket.
- The QML plugin shrinks to the icon with its status dot. A click runs `joma panel`.
  The plugin no longer polls `joma quick --json` every 15 seconds: Joma pushes the
  status.
- Cost: Joma moves from GPUI 0.2.2 on crates.io, which has no layer shell, to a pinned
  revision of Zed's git repository, as already done for gliff. The first attempt in Zed
  was reverted (#32651) and later reintroduced (#35610), so I check it on Hyprland
  before building on it.
- If the layer shell does not work well enough, the fallback is a normal floating window
  that Hyprland places under the bar with a window rule (like the old `joma quick`).

Alternative: keep the QML panel and keep growing it. It looks native in the shell, but it
is a second interface to maintain, and it only sees what the socket exposes.

- [ ] A:

**Q2. What the panel shows.**

Proposal, about 420×560 px:

- **Top:** your name, the status dot, buttons for invisible, settings and pop-out.
- **Middle:** a search field, then contacts as now (pinned, unread, online, recent).
- **Click a contact:** the conversation opens in the panel (last messages, composer,
  call, share and file buttons); Esc goes back to the list.
- **Incoming call:** the panel opens by itself with answer and decline, even when
  closed.

- [ ] A:

**Q3. Pop-out and pop-in.**

- **Pop-out** (button in the panel, or Ctrl+Shift+O): the panel closes and the full
  window opens on the current workspace, on the same conversation.
- **Pop-in** (button in the full window's top bar, or Ctrl+Shift+O again): the window
  closes and Joma goes back to the bar.
- **Closing the full window** (Super+W or Ctrl+W) pops it in, without quitting.
- **Ctrl+Q** really quits (the dot turns red).

GPUI ends the app when its last window closes; today Joma avoids that by hiding the
window in `special:joma`. With the panel there is a way out: Joma keeps an invisible
layer surface open, so no window is needed. If that does not hold, Joma keeps hiding the
window as it does now.

- [ ] A:

**Q4. Global shortcuts.**

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Super+Alt+M | open or close the panel (as now) |
| Super+Alt+Shift+M | open the full window, or bring it back |

Joma registers them through the Hyprland binding file, after asking (see Q12).

- [ ] A:

# B. Start, settings

**Q5. Start at login, in the bar.**

- A systemd user unit, `joma.service`, tied to the graphical session.
  - Omarchy starts the session with uwsm, so this is the standard way.
  - It also restarts Joma if it crashes, which a `exec-once` line does not do.
- "Start at login" in the settings turns the unit on or off.
- "Start in the bar" is on by default; off opens the full window at start.
- The service's journal (`journalctl --user -u joma`) replaces the log file.

Defaults I propose: start at login **on** once installed from a package, **off** with
`scripts/install.sh`.

- [ ] A:

**Q6. Settings, as a view of the full window (gear in the panel and the top bar).**

Sections:

- **General:** start at login, start in the bar, invisible, notifications (sound, show
  the text or only the sender), download folder, automatic download limit (20 MB).
- **Appearance:** follows the Omarchy theme (as now); font size.
- **Shortcuts:** the list, editable later.
- **Quick messages:** the list (today only `quick.toml`).
- **About:** version, check for updates (see Q14).

Everything saves to `~/.config/joma/config.toml`. `quick.toml` stays for the
favourites and the removed list, which change often.

- [ ] A:

# C. Contacts, chats, account

**Q7. A contacts page.**

- The list of all contacts with:
  - name, username, ID (copy), status;
  - date added;
  - a shared-conversation link.
- Actions:
  - **local nickname:** a name only you see, which beats theirs;
  - **favourite;**
  - **remove:** the current flow;
  - **block:** Jami's ban: they cannot write or call;
  - **unblock.**
- Pending requests, received and sent, with accept, decline and cancel.

- [ ] A:

**Q8. Deleting chats.**

Jami keeps conversations in a git repository copied on every member's devices, so no
client can erase the other side's copy.

- **Clear history** removes the messages on your devices only. The contact stays.
- **Delete conversation:** you leave it and its data goes from your devices (today:
  "delete for good" in the removed list).

The confirmation says "only on your devices".

- [ ] A:

**Q9. Your account.**

- **Profile:** name, picture (Jami supports one; Joma does not show pictures yet),
  username (as now).
- **Devices:**
  - the list of devices on the account, with name, ID and whether it is this one;
  - rename;
  - revoke a lost device;
  - **link a new device:** Jami's linking with a PIN or QR code.
- **Backup:** export the account to a file (with its password), so it can be restored
  on another machine. Recommended, since a Jami account lives only on its devices.
- **Password:** set or change the account password.

- [ ] A:

**Q10. Multiple accounts.**

- An account switcher at the top of the panel and of the window, with the unread count
  on each. All accounts stay connected, so messages and calls arrive on every one.
- **Add:** create, import from a backup file, or link from another device (Q9).
- **Remove:** from this machine only, after a reminder to back up.
- **The bar dot** sums them up: green when any account has unread messages, red when
  none is online.
- **Notifications** say which account they are for.
- **Pending question:** one list per account (switcher), or one list merging everyone
  with a small account mark? I propose per account, simpler and clearer; merged later
  if you miss it.

- [ ] A:

# D. Packaging and updates

**Q11. From scripts to a package, in steps.**

1. **AUR first: `joma-messenger-bin`.**
   - It installs a binary built by GitHub Actions at each tag, plus icons, launcher,
     the systemd unit and the plugin.
   - The `-bin` variant avoids every machine compiling GPUI (minutes and gigabytes).
   - Installed with `omarchy pkg aur add joma-messenger-bin`; it depends on
     `jami-daemon` (in Arch's `extra`).
2. **Updates:** `omarchy update` updates the AUR packages too, so Joma updates with
   the system. No updater of its own.
3. **Later, the Omarchy repository** (`pkgs.omarchy.org`, already in your
   `pacman.conf`). It is maintained by the Omarchy team: it needs a stable public
   release and their consent. To propose once Joma has a few months of use.

Both the AUR and Omarchy's repository need public sources: the repository becomes
public (GPL-3.0-or-later, as declared). Before then, a review for anything personal in
the history.

- [ ] A:

**Q12. The bar plugin from a package.**

The shell loads plugins only from its own folder (owned by the `omarchy` package) and
from `~/.config/omarchy/plugins`: a system package cannot add one by itself.

Proposal:

- The package puts the plugin in `/usr/share/joma/omarchy-plugin/`.
- At the first start, Joma asks: "Add Joma to the bar and the Super+Alt+M shortcut?"
  On yes, it:
  - links the plugin into `~/.config/omarchy/plugins`;
  - places it with `omarchy plugin enable io.github.dzanaga.joma-quick --section right`;
  - adds the binding;
  - enables the unit.
- **Settings → Integration** shows what is installed, with buttons to add or remove
  each piece.
- **Later:** propose to Omarchy a system folder for plugins from packages
  (`/usr/share/omarchy/plugins.d`), which would make that step automatic.

- [ ] A:

**Q13. Development and test builds.**

`scripts/install.sh` stays for development: it installs over the package in
`~/.local/bin`, and Settings → About says "development build". Tags `vX.Y.Z` make the
releases; GitHub Actions builds the binary for the AUR.

- [ ] A:

**Q14. In-app update notice?**

With pacman updating Joma, a check of its own is not needed. I propose only a line in
About ("installed with pacman / development build").

- [ ] A:

# E. Order

**Q15. Proposed order.**

| | What | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| J6 | Living in the bar: GPUI from git, layer-shell panel, pop-out/in, shortcuts, systemd unit, start at login / in the bar | the biggest change in daily use; the rest builds on it |
| J7 | Settings and management: settings view, contacts page, clearing and deleting chats, profile, devices, backup | needs the new window structure |
| J8 | Multiple accounts | touches the whole model: after J7, when the views are stable |
| J9 | Packaging: public repository, GitHub Actions, AUR `-bin`, first-run integration; later the Omarchy repository | when Joma is worth installing on someone else's machine |

- [ ] A:
